1. Mason Currey, [Making Art and Making a Living: Adventures in Funding a Creative Life](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=c75346762cf76243155df52a7f120e4f492e6d8eae6035498542cbfed7e9101c&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92867&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=16696ef2f82a0d212be03cba8c1820fb&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=8ae8059774ad9cbe07e7bb0f82eb9907). The best overall book I know on the different methods top artists have used to keep themselves going financially. It is perhaps more anecdotal and less theoretical than I would prefer, still a nice work.
2. Mangol Bayat, [Mysticism and Dissent: Socioreligious Dissent in Qajar Iran](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=8a3cb7af0c4e851e2fe7af682f4e2f4ae2a851b43b2c7862022d1500beca5d79&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92867&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=86453c4773ce17ee842549b9ae8591ba&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=8ae8059774ad9cbe07e7bb0f82eb9907). A very good, clear, and useful book on different dissident religiouis developments in Iran, leading up to the Bahai faith. Recommended, one of the best books I have found for grappling with the history of current Iran.
3. Lena Dunham, [Famesick: A Memoir](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=18ccb8f9f39b98c2e7ac9e5a7d02635acee11579672b5ea46b83ede2301d6fd0&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92867&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=ea64c7607431dc422759dd1c5751d5f8&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=8ae8059774ad9cbe07e7bb0f82eb9907). Not exactly my thing, so I did not finish it. But it is pretty good, so if you are tempted give it a try.
4. Iain Pears, [Parallel Lives: A Love Story from a Lost Continent](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=6bb601d5bb3af9897787c5854424810620c22e497993ccb7359c33593de265b1&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92867&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=a96ea77c89cf488e71ce10d6abe694f3&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=8ae8059774ad9cbe07e7bb0f82eb9907). A delightful story/indirect memoir, telling the tale of the lives and marriage of Frances Haskell, the British art historian, and Larissa Salmina Haskell, a Russian woman who survived the siege of Leningrad as a girl. Pears had the full cooperation of Larissa, at an age where she doesn't give a damn any more. This story truly comes to life, and that is helped by Pears's background as a writer of very good fiction.
5. [Lázár](https://marginalrevolution.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=3dcd054c96bc7f8ea9896567b1e010339ef461d2f115da6274b6c3dfe177e0ed&blog_id=42693868&post_id=92867&user_id=262258391&subs_id=225460721&signature=13f9d5f5bdb2863d0cc2f1518b627ce0&email_name=new-post&user_email=ishan.mail@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=8ae8059774ad9cbe07e7bb0f82eb9907), by Nelio Biedermann. An excellent novel of ideas, in the style of earlier Continental literature, by a 23-year-old Swiss phenom. It is very good in German, I have not sampled the translation.
